blueprint_topic: Management of Care — timely specialist kidney-care referral for CKD progression/complications
stem: An adult with established chronic kidney disease has an eGFR of 27 mL/min/1.73 m² and persistent hyperkalemia despite appropriate initial management. Which plan is most consistent with current KDIGO guidance?

options.A: Initiate referral to specialist kidney care now while continuing appropriate management of the potassium abnormality and other CKD complications.
options.B: Continue primary-care management and arrange specialist referral if the eGFR later falls below 15 mL/min/1.73 m² or kidney-replacement therapy becomes imminent.
options.C: Continue treatment of the hyperkalemia and postpone specialist referral until the serum potassium returns to the reference range on repeated testing.
options.D: Begin kidney-replacement-therapy education now and arrange specialist referral after the client has selected a dialysis or transplant pathway.

rationale: A is correct. KDIGO 2024 Practice Point 5.1.1 directs referral of adults with CKD to specialist kidney care in the circumstances listed in Figure 48. Figure 48 explicitly includes eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m² and persistent abnormalities of serum potassium as referral circumstances. The figure links these triggers to goals such as further evaluation/management, management of CKD complications, and planning/preparation for kidney-replacement therapy when appropriate. B is incorrect because KDIGO does not require waiting for eGFR below 15 or imminent KRT when referral criteria are already present. C is incorrect because persistent potassium abnormality is itself a referral circumstance rather than a reason to delay referral until corrected. D is incorrect because specialist referral supports evaluation, complication management, and KRT planning and therefore should not be deferred until after the client independently selects a modality.
educational_objective: Recognize specialist kidney-care referral triggers in established CKD, including eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m² and persistent serum-potassium abnormalities, and coordinate referral before dialysis is necessarily imminent.
source_document_title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease
source_version_date: Published 2024; current KDIGO CKD guideline suite rechecked 2026-08-20. KDIGO's March 17, 2026 focused-update announcement is limited to Chapter 3; this item relies on Chapter 5 referral guidance.
source_locator: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline — Chapter 5, Section 5.1 Referral to specialist kidney care services, Practice Point 5.1.1 and Figure 48, printed page S255/PDF file page 140: refer adults with CKD to specialist kidney care in the circumstances listed in Figure 48. Figure 48 includes eGFR <30 mL/min per 1.73 m² and persistent abnormalities of serum potassium among referral circumstances; stated referral goals include further evaluation/management, management of CKD complications, and planning/preparation for KRT. KDIGO March 17, 2026 focused-update announcement states the update focuses on Chapter 3, not Chapter 5.
source_claim_supported: Current KDIGO guidance directly supports specialist kidney-care referral for adults with CKD when eGFR is below 30 mL/min/1.73 m² or persistent serum-potassium abnormalities are present, without waiting until dialysis is imminent.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care — Referrals, Collaboration with Multidisciplinary Team, Case Management, and Continuity of Care: identify findings requiring referral, collaborate with specialty services, coordinate timely referrals, communicate significant findings, and follow unresolved care needs.
pdf_visual_verification: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline printed page S255/PDF file page 140 was visually verified by screenshot on 2026-08-20; Practice Point 5.1.1 and Figure 48 visibly showed eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² and persistent serum-potassium abnormalities as referral circumstances. Relevant NCSBN 2026 Management of Care referral/collaboration content had been visually verified earlier in this audit session.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'CKD eGFR below 30 persistent hyperkalemia nephrology referral specialist kidney care' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Retained the KDIGO referral construct and exact sourced eGFR threshold but removed must/only-style cueing. The rebuilt distractors test realistic delays: waiting for kidney failure/KRT imminence, waiting for potassium normalization despite a persistent abnormality, and postponing specialist involvement until after modality selection.

option_audit.A: Correct; both eGFR <30 and persistent potassium abnormality are explicit Figure 48 referral circumstances.
option_audit.B: Plausible late-referral error; incorrect because the current client already meets explicit referral circumstances before eGFR <15 or imminent KRT.
option_audit.C: Plausible stabilize-before-referral error; incorrect because persistent serum-potassium abnormality itself supports referral.
option_audit.D: Plausible KRT-sequencing error; incorrect because specialist kidney care participates in evaluation, complication management, and KRT planning rather than beginning only after modality choice.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All four alternatives contain comparable referral/sequencing detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel management plans for the same CKD referral scenario.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after KDIGO source-based audit and targeted repository search.
